Executive Summary The transition to high-performance buildings depends on a skilled workforce that can design, install, and maintain advanced building technologies. Employers across the buildings sector report persistent difficulties in hiring and retaining qualified workers, highlighting skill gaps (U.S. Department of Energy 2025). This report shares findings from a national survey of building energy performance and related contractors that was designed to better understand why companies hire and train workers, what they look for in new hires, and what helps or hinders their ability to invest in training. The findings can help building energy workforce development program administrators craft programs and outreach strategies that reflect and respond to the needs, perspectives, and realities of contractors. The survey targeted contractors that primarily complete energy performance improvement projects in buildings. Eligible respondents included business owners, decision makers, and employees across trades such as heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC); insulation; electrical work; plumbing; and building performance. A total of 209 individuals completed the survey, located in 37 U.S. states; Washington, D.C.; Guam; and the Marshall Islands.
